round1_findings_retested.finding: disclosure 'defect_found_during_rework' - harness.post retries only transport-level failures (max 3) because this machine's loopback sometimes refuses the first connect to a fresh httptest server
round1_findings_retested.how_verified: Read main.go:219-241 and judged it on three axes. (a) Confined to transport errors: only h.ts.Client().Do(req) returning a non-nil error reaches 'continue'; a response of any status is returned on the first attempt, unchanged, so no 401/403/409/500 can be retried into a different status and no product behaviour is masked. (b) It cannot flip a result by inventing a success: after three failed attempts post returns (0, errText), and every consumer asserts a concrete status (== 200 or == 401 or == 403), so status 0 fails rather than passing. (c) Side effects: the retried body is byte-identical including command_id, and the domain layer treats a repeated command_id as a replay, so a retry cannot double-execute a command; in practice every call site in this suite is host.status or an idempotent replay. VERDICT on the disclosure: honest and correctly scoped. ONE CORRECTION: the code comment's claim that 'Assertion outcomes must not depend on that' is not fully true. In one of my 21 runs (the first M-N2 application) BOOT-HOST-CONFIGURE-NEVER-ECHOES-SECRET and BOOT-HOST-CONFIGURE-REFUSED-UNTIL-HANDLER-CARD both failed although that mutation has no causal path to them, and the identical mutation passed 144/144 on three subsequent runs. The retry absorbs a single refused connect but gives up after 3 attempts spaced 50ms, and three consecutive refusals still flip two assertions. All ten UNMUTATED runs were byte-identical (sha 7195a132), so the observed rate is roughly 1 in 11 and it is an availability nuisance (a false FAIL), never a false PASS. A false FAIL is not a security defect, but the wording overstates the fix.

mutations_the_verifier_ran.assessment: The reply-direction grading the rework added protects the SUCCESS path only. Every frame that a handler refuses is answered by errorFrame(), and nothing in the suite asserts what bytes that error reply contains. Under this mutation the raw request - which for NATIVE_CREDENTIAL_IMPORT_REQUEST carries credential_value in cleartext - is written straight back down the pipe. Impact is bounded: the only peer that can open the pipe is a process of the same OS user (pipe DACL is one SID, PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS, FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE), and it is receiving the bytes it itself sent, so this is not a cross-principal disclosure. It does defeat the stated invariant 'nothing that crosses this boundary is echoed back', and it is the exact shape a later card would turn into a real leak the moment a bridge reply is logged, forwarded into an event, or relayed to a renderer. Graded minor for this card, must be closed by the card that wires the shipped clients.

independent_review_round2.reservations: ACCEPT_WITH_RESERVATIONS. The substance of round 1's rejection is genuinely fixed and I verified it with my own eyes and my own mutations, not the receipt's: all twelve of the required-mapping mutations (M-A through M-J plus M-N1) are caught with precise, single-purpose failed-id sets; build, vet, gofmt, ten byte-identical unmutated harness runs (PASS / 144 assertions / 0 failures / the same single not_verified item) and the registered binding all reproduce; my own process/token census confirms the not_verified claim and confirms it more strongly than the check's capped scan; the neighbours hold at 49 and 136; nothing outside write_scope moved in this round; and the four remaining numbered gaps are all evidence-quality, not exploitable holes. Two things keep this short of ACCEPT, and the verdict rule is explicit that they must. First, hashes do not all match: receipt.json pins a stale self-hash (e1625390 for what is actually fc1bcbc1), the one artifact an EVIDENCE gate exists to self-verify. Second, four mutations I wrote are not caught, all of them in code the rework itself introduced: M-K (the serve path can answer a refused frame by echoing the request payload, credential_value included, with the suite green twice running), M-N2 (the production default peer lookup can be replaced by a stub that always says 'same user' - the wiring line that round 1's blocker turned on is still unpinned, though the comparison and the OS answer now are pinned), and M-O/M-O2 (the staged-withdrawal closures for credential-import and workspace-choose are never driven through a refusal, so fix 2's 'root revoked, selection withdrawn' claim is evidenced for one of three handlers).
